items.title: Mike De Lay Interview, 1958-09-02
items.q: I remember Lee Collins. Oh, yeah. Oh, he was one of my favorites. I'd say in later years, right after I began playing, he was really one of my favorites.

ctx.x: I've been asked about some of the trumpet players. Do you remember Sam Morgan's band?

Sam Morgan, yes, Sam Morgan. I remember Sam Morgan very well. And I remember, just trumpet players? I remember Lee Collins. Oh, yeah. Oh, he was one of my favorites. I'd say in later years, right after I began playing, he was really one of my favorites. You know, of course, Lewis Armstrong on top all the time. I guess anybody else in those days felt the same. But Lee Collins was really one of my favorites. I'd say like in the years, beginning around 30. And even in 29, I was a short pass. No, no, it was before…
Is that the Astoria Hotel, that place?

items.title: Mike De Lay Interview, 1970-11-14
items.q: one of my number one was Lee Collins. Lee Collins. Oh, I thought nobody had a drive like that guy.

ctx.x: Mike, when you were playing up, do you consider the best cornet player?

Oh, that's a kind of hard thing. Sure. To say, because you know the reason why, when I was a kid, you're talking about it? Yeah. Because I was listening to the cornet and trumpets all my, what's that cornet then, that damn night. All my days, I just loved it. My mother wouldn't buy me one. She wouldn't buy me a violin. I didn't want to buy me. But anyway, I had my, well, before Ludd, John Tron came along, I was crazy about my teacher, Manuel Perez. He had such a name around there, you know, around him. He, when…
I said, plenty gold on the lawn socks. No, I didn't know.
